hazards.name: Lack of pedestrian walkways
hazards.description: There are no paved sidewalks on either side of the road, forcing pedestrians to walk on the grass or in the travel lane.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground and middle ground along the roadway edges

hazards.name: Excessive crossing distance
hazards.description: The multi-lane road and wide median create a very long unprotected crossing distance for pedestrians with no marked crosswalks.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the entire width of the roadway

hazards.name: Wide Roadway
hazards.description: The multi-lane road design encourages higher vehicle speeds and creates a long crossing distance for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Lack of Crossings
hazards.description: No marked pedestrian crossings are visible along this stretch of road.

hazards.name: Pavement Degradation
hazards.description: Visible cracking and wear in the asphalt surface could pose a trip hazard if pedestrians cross mid-block.

hazards.name: Lack of lighting
hazards.description: No visible street lighting may reduce safety and comfort for pedestrians at night.

hazards.name: Reduced natural surveillance
hazards.description: Dense vegetation and a solid fence create a blank frontage, limiting visibility from adjacent buildings.

hazards.name: Absence of crossing facilities
hazards.description: There are no marked crosswalks or pedestrian refuge areas visible, making crossing the wide street potentially hazardous.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the roadway in the mid-block section.

hazards.name: Missing sidewalk on opposite side
hazards.description: The left side of the roadway lacks any paved pedestrian infrastructure, forcing pedestrians to walk on the grass or in the travel lane.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: Large, dense bushes at the corner of the driveway entrance block sightlines between pedestrians on the sidewalk and drivers exiting the parking area.
hazards.location_in_image: Left-center foreground, adjacent to the sidewalk and driveway junction

hazards.name: Unmarked Driveway Crossing
hazards.description: The wide driveway lacks markings or a continuous sidewalk material, which may lead to confusion regarding pedestrian priority.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground, where the asphalt driveway crosses the concrete sidewalk path

hazards.name: Absence of Sidewalks
hazards.description: There are no paved walkways for pedestrians, forcing them to walk on the grass or the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Both sides of the visible road

hazards.name: High-speed road geometry
hazards.description: The wide, straight road design with multiple lanes encourages higher vehicle speeds, increasing risk for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Unmarked wide driveway crossing
hazards.description: The lack of markings across the wide driveway entrance fails to define a clear pedestrian path, increasing the risk of vehicle-pedestrian conflicts.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground where the sidewalk meets the asphalt driveway

hazards.name: Sightline obstructions
hazards.description: Mature trees and a large sign on the left side of the driveway may partially obscure sightlines between pedestrians and drivers exiting the facility.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the driveway entrance

hazards.name: Missing Sidewalks
hazards.description: There is no paved walkway for pedestrians on either side of the road, forcing anyone on foot to walk in the grass or on the roadway shoulder.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground and background along the road edges

hazards.name: High-Speed Roadway Design
hazards.description: The wide, multi-lane configuration with minimal roadside friction and no pedestrian safety features encourages high vehicle speeds.

hazards.name: Lack of Controlled Crossings
hazards.description: There are no visible marked crosswalks or signals to facilitate safe crossing of the wide arterial road.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the entire visible stretch of the road

hazards.name: Wide crossing distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross multiple lanes of traffic without a refuge or marked crossing despite the presence of a crossing warning sign.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the main roadway near the yellow pedestrian sign

hazards.name: Driveway Conflict Point
hazards.description: A driveway on the left intersects the sidewalk, creating potential conflict points between pedestrians and vehicles entering or exiting the parking area.

hazards.name: Lack of Protected Crossing
hazards.description: There are no marked crosswalks visible across the two-lane roadway, forcing pedestrians to cross without designated protection or priority.

hazards.name: Faded Crosswalk Markings
hazards.description: The zebra markings on the crosswalk appear worn, reducing visibility to drivers.

hazards.name: Unmarked Transit Crossing
hazards.description: A bus stop is present without any marked crossing or pedestrian warning signs, creating risk for transit users crossing the road.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Crossings
hazards.description: No marked crossings are visible to facilitate safe passage across the wide roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the foreground and midground roadway.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install zebra-striped crosswalks with appropriate signage to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way in the school zone.

interventions.title: Speed Humps or Tables
interventions.description: Implement physical speed reduction measures to ensure motorists adhere to the 15 mph school zone speed limit.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct curb extensions at potential crossing points to reduce crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Install Street Lighting
interventions.description: Add pedestrian-scale street lighting to improve visibility and safety after dark.

interventions.title: Improve Frontage Transparency
interventions.description: Replace the solid fence with a more open design to allow for better natural surveillance and a more engaging pedestrian environment.

interventions.title: Lane Narrowing with Bike Lanes
interventions.description: Repurpose excess roadway width to include marked bike lanes, which naturally narrows travel lanes and slows traffic.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Installation
interventions.description: Construct a continuous, ADA-compliant concrete sidewalk along the roadway to provide a dedicated space for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Marked Crosswalks and Pedestrian Signals
interventions.description: Install high-visibility crosswalks and pedestrian countdown signals at the nearest intersection to provide safe crossing opportunities.

interventions.title: Pedestrian-Scale Lighting
interventions.description: Add lighting specifically oriented toward the new walkway to improve visibility and safety at night.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk
interventions.description: Install marked crosswalks with signage to provide safe crossing opportunities.

interventions.title: Install Pedestrian-Scale Lighting
interventions.description: Add street lamps along the sidewalk to ensure the path is well-lit for nighttime use.

interventions.title: Improve Frontage Permeability
interventions.description: Encourage more transparent fencing or additional landscaping to reduce the 'blank wall' effect and improve the pedestrian experience.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Warning Signage
interventions.description: Install signage to alert drivers to the potential presence of pedestrians crossing.

interventions.title: Marked Midblock Crossing
interventions.description: Install a high-visibility marked crosswalk with a pedestrian refuge island in the existing median and appropriate signage.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Hybrid Beacon (PHB)
interventions.description: Install a signalized crossing to allow pedestrians to safely cross the multi-lane thoroughfare.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Add a median or refuge island to reduce the unprotected crossing distance on this wide road.

interventions.title: Lane Narrowing
interventions.description: Reduce lane widths to naturally slow traffic speeds and provide space for other infrastructure like bike lanes.

interventions.title: Vegetation Management
interventions.description: Prune or thin dense bushes to improve sightlines between the sidewalk and the building frontage.

interventions.title: Road Diet
interventions.description: Narrowing the travel lanes by adding a protected bike lane or widening the buffer to reduce vehicle speeds.

interventions.title: Mid-block Crossing
interventions.description: Installation of a high-visibility marked crosswalk, potentially with a pedestrian refuge island or RRFB.

interventions.title: Midblock Pedestrian Crossing
interventions.description: Install a high-visibility marked crosswalk with a pedestrian refuge island in the existing wide median.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Extension
interventions.description: Construct a new sidewalk on the left side of the street to provide a continuous and safe pedestrian network on both sides of the roadway.

interventions.title: Mid-block Crosswalk
interventions.description: Install a high-visibility marked crosswalk with pedestrian-actuated warning beacons to facilitate safe crossing to the institution.

interventions.title: Traffic Calming
interventions.description: Introduce speed humps or curb extensions to reduce vehicle speeds and shorten the pedestrian crossing distance.

interventions.title: Continuous Sidewalk Treatment
interventions.description: Extend the concrete sidewalk material across the driveway to physically and visually reinforce pedestrian priority.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Markings
interventions.description: Add crosswalk markings across the driveway entrance to alert drivers to the presence of pedestrians.

interventions.title: Marked Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install high-visibility marked crosswalks at regular intervals or key desire lines to provide safe crossing points.

interventions.title: Bicycle Infrastructure
interventions.description: Adding a marked bike lane would narrow the travel lanes for cars, naturally slowing traffic while providing space for cyclists.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Buffers
interventions.description: Plant street trees between the new sidewalk and the roadway to provide a physical and psychological buffer from traffic.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk Markings
interventions.description: Paint a ladder or zebra-style crosswalk across the driveway to clearly define the pedestrian path and reinforce pedestrian priority.

interventions.title: Tactile Warning Surfaces
interventions.description: Install detectable warning surfaces (truncated domes) on both sides of the driveway to alert visually impaired users of the transition to a vehicular area.

interventions.title: Driveway Narrowing
interventions.description: Use curb extensions or paint to narrow the driveway throat, reducing pedestrian crossing distance and slowing turning vehicles.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Completion
interventions.description: Construct a sidewalk on the right side of the road to provide a continuous and safe pedestrian network on both sides of the street.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Crossing Improvements
interventions.description: Install high-visibility marked crosswalks, potentially with Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons (PHB) or RRFBs, to provide safe crossing points.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Buffer Zone
interventions.description: Add a planting strip with street trees between the new sidewalk and the roadway to provide physical and psychological separation from traffic.

interventions.title: Traffic Calming Measures
interventions.description: Implement speed humps or cushions to reduce vehicle speeds along this straight stretch of road, improving safety for all users.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Lighting
interventions.description: Add pedestrian-scale lighting to improve visibility and safety for people walking at night.

interventions.title: Wayfinding Signage
interventions.description: Since the frontage is blank and provides few landmarks, wayfinding can help pedestrians navigate to nearby destinations.

interventions.title: New Sidewalk Construction
interventions.description: Install a paved sidewalk on the right side of the street to provide a continuous pedestrian network.

interventions.title: Mid-block Pedestrian Crossing
interventions.description: Install a high-visibility marked crosswalk with pedestrian warning signage near the bus stop.
